html:
SMTO-PSM-0005 — SMTO couldn't use that Parameter Store request

GUID: 9f3c9468-c66c-4ada-a323-c1c2246538f3
Slug: parameter-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • A request to look up or change a saved parameter was written in a form SMTO can't accept, so SMTO stopped before doing it. Nothing was read, saved or deleted by this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In your message, type @ and pick the parameter from the list that appears, instead of typing its name by hand. SMTO only accepts the exact saved name; the list inserts that name for you, while nicknames (aliases) only help you find it.
  2. If you asked the Agent to look up, change or delete a parameter, say plainly which one and what to do, for example "show the parameter @my_server" or "delete @old_token". This error happens when a lookup or change request mixes options that don't belong together, and a clear one-action request avoids that.
  3. Open the More options menu (⋯) at the top of the chat, choose Parameter Store, and use Search parameters… to confirm the parameter exists and see its exact name. Seeing the exact name in Parameter Store tells you what to type after @.

What success looks like

  • The Agent shows or changes the parameter you asked about without this error appearing again.

If it still fails

  • Don't keep sending the same request unchanged. Open Technical details, select Copy error details, and send them with your request text to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Parameter Store reference used an unsupported key, or a parameters.inspect / parameters.manage call combined fields its operation does not accept (for example get without key, or delete with extra fields).

What this means

  • Prompt reference parsing rejects unsupported key syntax/length, or parameter-tool validation rejects missing/contradictory operation fields. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Prompt reference parsing rejects unsupported key syntax/length, or parameter-tool validation rejects missing/contradictory operation fields.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish an invalid @key from get/search/delete argument conflicts using the owning operation schema.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact message in Technical details: "get requires key", "query applies only to list/search", "key and include_audit apply only to get" and "delete accepts only operation and key" come from src/agent_runtime/skills/parameters/tools.py. Resend the call with only the fields that operation accepts, and use the exact normalized key shown in the @ palette rather than an alias.
  • Select the exact main key and correct the reported operation fields against the current schema; keep private values out of prompt syntax.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact main key and operation-specific fields validate without guessed aliases.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
